causal_chain: Firmware v4.2 meters, rolled out 2026-06, report register readings in 0.1 m3 units, while older v3.x firmware reports in whole m3 units (E-14).

Billing import rejects these misflagged AMI reads with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, affecting 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-12).

Customers dispute these bills, contributing to the dispute-ticket surge whose onset in August coincides with BV-17's deployment (E-01, E-13).

proposal.summary: The dispute surge investigation began from SH-CS's request (CL-01) for an auto-answering/auto-fixing AI agent, but response-time data (E-02) ruled out slow handling as the cause. Evidence established that monthly disputes doubled from ~600 (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260 (Aug-Sep, E-01), and after an earlier framing (PD-1@v1, blaming route shortfalls and ACTUAL-read defects) was invalidated by E-12, the successor problem (PD-1@v2) confirmed the mechanism: validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13), lacking unit scaling for v4.2 firmware's 0.1 m3 register units (E-14), causes 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills to be rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12, corroborated by E-15/E-16/E-17); the cause of the remaining ACTUAL-read disputes (1785/3025, E-04) is still unknown. A proposed release scope limited to two monitoring capabilities (dispute-volume trend, validation-rule rejection-impact monitoring, per SD-2) was evaluated for release, but the release decision is HOLD: automated Layer-1 verification failed due to missing monitor data (2374 records), a duplicate-semantics check failure, and an inconsistency between a stated exclusion rationale and the actual (resolved) status of VOB-U-FULL-POPULATION-SCOPE. Several known limitations remain regardless of release status, including an unconfirmed seasonal baseline, no automated bill correction capability, no tool to deploy the BV-17 fix itself, and open questions about ACTUAL-read causation and handoff integrity.
